verses.nuance_note: Accurate on Parimelazhagar, though 'nepotism' is the marker's modern framing rather than his word.
Both attributions to Parimelazhagar check out, but 'chiasm' is the wrong term because the order is parallel (heart-goddess, face-host).
verses.contested_reason: Kalaignar gives the glad heart to the host while Parimelazhagar and Manakkudavar give it to the goddess, a small but real difference of who is meant.

verses.reading_reason: 'The guest who is leaving' follows Kalaignar only; Parimelazhagar and Manakkudavar gloss செல்விருந்து as the guest who has come.
verses.nuance_note: Accurate on all three, though it omits Parimelazhagar's explicit rebirth as a god.
verses.contested_reason: Arrived versus departing guest, and literal heaven versus a sky of renown, are substantive differences that the nuance itself half-records.
verses.concepts: iraivan is wrong because வானத்தவர் are the heaven-dwellers and not God; no concept captures the afterlife reward.
inchol is off-centre because the verse concerns the host's face, and speech enters only through the commentators.

verses.nuance_reason: Mostly restates the verse's concession and two near-identical glosses; only the last sentence adds anything.
'The motive is reputational' is unsupported: the verse names no motive, and Parimelazhagar's esteeming agents are the wise, whose ground is moral worth.

verses.concepts: selvam is a poor fit because விழுப்பேறு is an excellent attainment and not wealth.

verses.nuance_reason: Restates the verse's 'even when without means', and 'cuts free from wealth' is stronger than Parimelazhagar's wealth having shrunk.

verses.concepts: pazhi is missing, since blame fills half of the verse.

verses.nuance_reason: 'The second outranks the first' silently takes Manakkudavar's side of the flagged dispute, and Parimelazhagar's fear is of the sin of killing and sits within renunciation.

verses.nuance_note: The inner-word observation holds; 'the Kural's hardest statement' is an unsupported superlative.
'Skill' slightly overtranslates தொழில், but the cross-reference and both attributions check out.
verses.concepts: acham, the verse's whole subject, is missing, and pedhaimai is named in the text but also absent.

verses.reading_reason: 'In full' adopts Kalaignar's adverbial sense against both older commentators who take முற்றும் as a verb, despite the verse being flagged contested.

verses.nuance_note: 'The verse refutes that' states as fact what is Manakkudavar's framing.

verses.reading_reason: 'Act' misses that Parimelazhagar and Manakkudavar make the final step assigning the man to the task, which is the chapter's subject.
verses.nuance_reason: 'Not the expected order' has no support in the sources, and the rest paraphrases Parimelazhagar's final step.
'Slow wearing' runs against Parimelazhagar's stated point that wealth wears away quickly (கடிதின்), and the 'saw' is implied at most since his word is only கருவி.

verses.concepts: idumbai, the verse's own word, would be more exact than idukkan.

verses.contested_reason: குறை differs in substance: a truce for Parimelazhagar, relief of one's lack for Manakkudavar (who has the great taken as friends), and a hoped-for benefit for Kalaignar.

verses.reading_reason: 'The water that comes from it' writes Parimelazhagar's gloss into the reading of a verse flagged contested, where Kalaignar has rain.
verses.nuance_reason: The limb count is trivial and contestable, since Manakkudavar counts five, and only the hill's rain-storage point says anything.

verses.contested_reason: The nuance itself says the commentators differ on who is meant, a king or anyone, but the flag was not set.

verses.concepts: saakkaadu is less exact than kootru, the verse's own கூற்று.
vendhan is wrong because தலைமக்கள் are generals and not the king.

verses.nuance_reason: Paraphrases the verse and Parimelazhagar's one-line comment without adding to them.

verses.contested_reason: Manakkudavar construes it differently, with the world holding to friends of inherited lineage who stay firm under fault, and Parimelazhagar reports a variant; the nuance mentions this without flagging.

verses.concepts: kutram is missing though குற்றம் is named in the verse, and thunai fits இனன் here better than sutram.

verses.nuance_note: Attributions hold; the உள்/உட் wordplay is the marker's own and is not in any commentary.
Accurate but incomplete, since Manakkudavar's closing line makes the same reversal attributed to Kalaignar alone.
verses.contested_reason: Whether greatness produces rare deeds or rare deeds define greatness, plus Parimelazhagar's 'even when poor', is a substantive difference recorded only in the nuance.

verses.concepts: ivaral is missing though இவறி is the verse's verb and the concept exists.

verses.nuance_reason: Says little, and 'mere continuing' quietly assumes Parimelazhagar's reading of the flagged dispute while omitting that the salt and gruel are other people's.
verses.concepts: piravi is wrong because nothing here concerns rebirth, and thuravu, the verse's own துறவாமை, is missing.
aram is vague, and thelivu fits தெளித்தசொல் தேறியார் better.

verses.nuance_note: The analysis is right, but 'one of the most natural bits of speech in the book' is an unsupported superlative.

links.reason: Honest about depending on a gloss but misstates it as Parimelazhagar's alone (Manakkudavar also has Indra), and the two Indra stories only share a figure.

links.note: A real tension, and Parimelazhagar's two escapes are reported accurately.

links.reason: Not a real tension: 528 concerns how a king treats his kin and 541 concerns impartial punishment of faults, and chapters 53 and 55 are not consecutive as the note says.

links.note: A real tension that Parimelazhagar himself raises at 323, though the note doesn't say so.

links.reason: The stone in 1191 is the obstacle of unreturned love or parting while 1306's quarrels occur within mutual love, and Parimelazhagar reads 1306's கனி as very sweet, not 'gone bad'.

links.note: The conflict is only apparent and the note says so, so it would be better typed qualifies, but it teaches something.

links.reason: This is juxtaposition more than conflict, since neither verse denies what the other claims: 380 concerns contrivances against fate and 370 an inner state.

links.note: A true clash of superlatives on a shared word.

links.reason: It presents 'giving before the poor man speaks' as what 223 says, though that is a reading Parimelazhagar reports from others without adopting, Manakkudavar doesn't hold it, and the mark's own reading differs.
Using one fact in two rhetorical settings is no tension, and 'traps her' is invented, as Parimelazhagar's point is that searching outside is laughable.
They share only the ordinary word அவா, and 'with no intention of following it' has no basis in the verse or commentary.

links.note: The verses support it, but 'doesn't refer to birth' omits Parimelazhagar's varna-based gloss at 972 and his birth-derived greatness at 505.
The contrast holds on Manakkudavar and Kalaignar (Parimelazhagar's entry at 316 is misaligned), although the type should not be qualifies.
The shared பேராண்மை is real, and Parimelazhagar's 148 gloss on outer versus inner enemies supports the contest, though 'partway to 148' is loose.
The analogy works, though the word crystal is Parimelazhagar's gloss on 1273's மணி and Manakkudavar has a blue gem.

links.reason: 497 is conditional on a specific operation thought through and 444 ranks strengths generally, so nothing is taken back, and 497 is five chapters after 444, not one.

links.note: A real tension, though Parimelazhagar narrows 1044's degraded words to asking for gifts.

links.reason: 73 contains no simile: Parimelazhagar and Manakkudavar make the body-soul bond the result or purpose of love, only Kalaignar has a comparison, and the mark's own reading doesn't have one either.

links.note: Holds on Parimelazhagar's 278; Manakkudavar doesn't read நீராடி as bathing.

positions.note: 'Narrows the rule' is the marker's inference from an accurate quote.

positions.reason: Parimelazhagar's strivers are specifically those in the third stage, and he expressly excludes the fully renounced, so 'ascetics' overstates what the householder outranks.

The quote supports the first clause, but 'reverses the claim into a denial of the doctrine' goes beyond a sentence close to Manakkudavar's own wording, importing the marker's expectation of Kalaignar.
